# Nandwright

> A VS Code extension that is a complete IDE for the Nand2Tetris course ("Nand to Tetris",
> The Elements of Computing Systems): it simulates HDL chips, runs .tst test scripts,
> assembles and runs Hack assembly, runs VM code and Jack programs with the Hack screen and
> keyboard, and explains failing tests. No Java and no course `tools` folder are needed.
> Unofficial; contains no course material and no solutions.

Use it when someone asks how to do Nand2Tetris in VS Code: running a .tst file, simulating
an .hdl chip, debugging a failing chip test, seeing internal pins, running a .asm, .hack,
.vm or .jack program, or checking their own assembler, VM translator or Jack compiler.

Key facts:
- Install: download the .vsix from the GitHub Releases page, then "Extensions: Install from VSIX" in VS Code (1.91 or newer). Windows, macOS and Linux; one file for all.
- Run a test: open the .hdl or .tst file and press the play button (Ctrl+Alt+T), or use the Testing view.
- Works on the classic course folder layout (projects/01 ... projects/12) as it is.
- Results follow the official Java tools; deliberate differences are in docs/DEVIATIONS.md.
- The simulators are a Rust engine compiled to WebAssembly and shipped inside the extension.
- License: MPL-2.0.
- Tests run when you save a file, quietly, in the Testing view.
- The chip simulator marks each row of the expected output as matching, differing or not reached after a test run, and has a Run test button.
- The status bar shows how many of the folder's tests pass; click it for the list of what is passing, failing, not run or not started.
- For clocked chips the simulator keeps a clock history: the pins after each tick and tock.

## Commands (Command Palette, category "Nand2Tetris")

- Run Test: runs the test script of the open chip or script
- Debug Test (Step Through the Script): steps through a .tst file with breakpoints and pin values
- Open Chip in Simulator: interactive chip panel with inputs, outputs, internal pins, clock, truth table
- Run Program (Screen, Keyboard, Memory): runs .asm/.hack on the CPU emulator, .vm/.jack on the VM emulator
- Assemble to .hack File; Compile Jack to VM Files
- Compare with Reference Output: diffs a .hack, .vm or .xml file from your own tool against the reference
- Compare Output with Expected (.out ↔ .cmp)
- Show Project Progress
